title: TAMs, Concierge and the Support Center

kcs.statement: A technical account manager (TAM) is a named AWS technical contact who gives proactive architecture, operations and cost guidance; Enterprise Support provides a designated TAM, while the legacy Enterprise On-Ramp plan gave only a pool of TAMs.
Enterprise-level plans add the Concierge Support Team for billing and account questions and Infrastructure Event Management help for planned launches and peak events.
AWS Support Center in the console is where you open and track support cases; on Basic Support you can open only account and billing cases, not technical ones.

problem_ideas: A company wants one named AWS engineer who knows its workloads: which plan is the minimum?
A finance team has complex invoicing questions across 200 accounts: which support team helps, and at which plan level?
A retailer plans a Super Bowl ad launch and wants AWS to help prepare: name the offering.
A Basic Support user wants to report an EC2 networking bug through Support Center: what happens?
Pool of TAMs versus designated TAM: map each to its plan.
Spot the false statement: 'Business Support+ includes a designated technical account manager.'
